source_text: Cum ergo hoc ita inconcussum sit, ut nulla queat argumentatione convelli; tu elige utrum mavis, et vel nostram, vel tuam constanter affirma sententiam; ut aut necessitati, aut voluntati imputes culpam. Cum autem dico, utrum mavis, non sic admoneo, quasi tua adhuc lateat opinio, qui crimina naturae per Manichaeum importare didicisti; sed ideo hoc commoneo, ut disputationis tuae veritas denotetur.
pass_a_gloss: Since therefore this is so unshaken that it can be torn by no argumentation; you choose which you prefer, and constantly affirm either our sentence or yours; so that you impute fault either to necessity or to will. But when I say which you prefer, I do not so advise as if your opinion still lies hidden, you who learned through Manichaeus to import charges of nature; but I warn this for this reason, that the truth of your disputation may be marked.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: Since this is so unshakable that no argument can overthrow it, choose whichever you prefer and consistently affirm either my statement or yours, so that you impute guilt either to necessity or to will. When I say “whichever you prefer,” I am not advising you as though your opinion were still hidden: you learned through Manichaeus to bring crimes into nature. I give this warning so that the truthfulness of your argument may be put on record.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
